P001.content: Responds well to warm white light (3000K) during evening hours. Blue light (5000K) in morning helps with alertness and recovery.
Medium light intensity (40-60%) preferred during the day. Dimmer lighting (20-30%) at night reduces agitation and improves sleep quality.
Responds positively to calm instrumental music, particularly classical compositions. Music helps reduce anxiety during medical procedures.
Upbeat, energetic music in the morning (120-130 BPM) helps with motivation and engagement. Slower tempo (60-80 BPM) recommended in evenings.
High intensity bright lighting (>80%) causes visible distress and overstimulation. Patient becomes agitated and restless within 5-10 minutes.
Heavy metal and loud rock music (>100dB) triggers anxiety and aggressive behavior. Completely counterproductive during therapy sessions.

P002.content: Prefers cooler color temperature (5500K) throughout the day. Finds warm lighting uncomfortable and associates it with fatigue.
High intensity lighting (70-80%) preferred during therapy sessions to maintain alertness. Regular intensity (50-60%) for general activities.
Traditional Spanish folk music has calming effect. Exposure to familiar music from home reduces stress levels significantly.
Rhythmic Latin music (90-110 BPM) improves mood and engagement during art therapy sessions. Maintains consistent tempo preference.
Warm color temperature (2700K) causes fatigue and drowsiness. Leads to reduced participation in therapy activities and poor engagement.
Slow, melancholic music (40-60 BPM) worsens mood and increases withdrawn behavior. Avoids classical and sad instrumental pieces.

P003.content: Soft, gentle lighting with warm color (2700K) creates safe, comforting environment. Harsh or bright lights cause distress.
Low to medium light intensity (30-50%) optimal for comfort. Avoid bright lighting above 60% intensity due to visual sensitivity.
Gentle, soothing classical music or nature sounds (piano, strings) have relaxing effect. Audiobook storytelling also very effective.
Slow, peaceful tempo (50-70 BPM) preferred. Sound levels should be kept moderate (40-50dB) to prevent overstimulation.
Harsh blue light (6000K+) combined with high intensity creates panic-like response. Patient becomes inconsolable and withdrawn for extended periods.
Loud, energetic music (>60dB) or sudden loud noises cause severe distress and trigger crying episodes. Sound sensitivity is significant concern.

P004.content: Neutral white light (4500K) works well for daytime activities. Supports natural circadian rhythm and maintains energy levels.
Bright lighting (65-80%) during activity and therapy sessions enhances focus. Moderate (45-55%) for rest periods between sessions.
Sports commentary and energetic pop/rock music (120-140 BPM) align with interests and boost mood. Motivates during recovery exercises.
Background ambient music during rest periods (70-90 BPM) helps with pain management. Avoids silence which can increase focus on discomfort.
Dim, low lighting (<40%) during daytime reduces motivation and increases fatigue. Patient shows poor participation in physical therapy when lighting is inadequate.
Quiet environments or silence increase focus on pain sensations. Leads to increased reports of discomfort and reduced engagement in recovery activities.

P005.content: Bright, cool white light (5000-5500K) during morning and afternoon. Promotes alertness and supports healthy sleep-wake cycle.
High light intensity (75-85%) during education/learning activities. Reduces to 50-60% during meal times and social activities.
Upbeat children's songs and age-appropriate music (110-130 BPM) boost mood and engagement. Singing along helps with emotional expression.
Variety in music selections prevents habituation. Rotates between pop, children's music, and instrumental pieces throughout the day.
